Opinion polling for the [[2010 Brazilian presidential election]] started as early as 2008. All polls conducted between 1 January 2010 and election day were registered in the [[Superior Electoral Court]] database, as required by electoral law.<ref>{{in lang|pt}} [http://noticias.terra.com.br/eleicoes/2010/noticias/0,,OI4392823-EI15311,00-Confira+o+calendario+eleitoral.html "Confira o calendário eleitoral 2010"]. Terra.</ref> The main nationwide polling institutes are Datafolha, [[IBOPE]], Vox Populi, and Sensus.

==Election information==
{{main|2010 Brazilian presidential election}}

The first round of the 2010 Brazilian presidential election was held on October 3, as part of the country's [[2010 Brazilian general election|general election]], with a second round between the two leading candidates on October 31. That happened because under Brazilian law, if none of the candidates receives more than a half of the valid votes, a run-off is held four weeks after the first round.<ref>Colitt, Raymond. [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSN3021637720100111?type=marketsNews "Key dates in Brazil's 2010 presidential race"]. [[Reuters]]. January 11, 2010.</ref> The leading candidate, [[Dilma Rousseff]], received 46.9% of the first-round vote, thereby making a second round necessary.

In the election, Brazilian citizens eligible to vote chose their successor to then-[[President of Brazil|President]] [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]], of the [[democratic socialist]]/[[social democratic]] [[Workers' Party (Brazil)|Workers' Party]]. According to the Constitution, the president is elected directly to a four-year term, with a limit of two terms. Lula was hence ineligible for a third term, since he was [[2002 Brazilian general election|elected in 2002]] and [[2006 Brazilian general election|re-elected in 2006]].<ref name=NYT>Barrionuevo, Alexei. [https://www.nytimes.com/2009/05/24/world/americas/24brazil.html?_r=1&scp=1&sq=Dilma%20Rousseff&st=cse "The Health of a Likely Presidential Candidate Comes Under Brazil's Microscope"]. ''[[The New York Times]]'', May 23, 2009. Accessed June 14, 2009.</ref> The 2010 election marked the first time since the end of the [[Brazilian military dictatorship|military dictatorship]] that Lula was not a candidate for the presidency.<ref name="Ray">Colitt, Raymond. [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSN3013312120100111?loomia_ow=t0:s0:a49:g43:r1:c0.500000:b29738878:z0 "Positions of Brazil's leading candidates"]. Reuters. January 11, 2010.</ref>

===Candidates overview===
Since the earliest polls for president, former [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]] Governor [[José Serra]] – candidate for the [[center-right]]<ref>{{cite journal |author= Freedom House |date= July 16, 2009 |title= Freedom in the World 2009 - Brazil |journal= [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees|UNHCR]] |url= http://unhcr.org/refworld/publisher,FREEHOU,,BRA,4a6452cb23,0.html |quote= In early 1994, Fernando Henrique Cardoso (...) forged a three-party, centre-right coalition around his Brazilian Social Democracy Party (PSDB). |author-link= Freedom House |access-date= May 14, 2010 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110724154058/http://unhcr.org/refworld/publisher,FREEHOU,,BRA,4a6452cb23,0.html |archive-date= July 24, 2011 |url-status= dead }}</ref> opposition group led by the [[centrism|centrist]]/[[Third Way (centrism)|Third Way]]<ref name="Col">Colitt, Raymond. [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSN1718245920091217 "Key names in Brazil's 2010 presidential race"]. Reuters. December 17, 2010.</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last= Segrillo |first= Angelo |year= 2004 |title= A confusão esquerda-direita no mundo pós-Muro de Berlim |trans-title= The left-right confusion in the post-Berlin Wall world |journal= Dados |volume= 47 |pages= 615–632 |issn= 0011-5258 |doi=10.1590/S0011-52582004000300006 | language= pt |quote= <!-- ORIGINAL PORTUGUESE TEXT: A maioria dos analistas classificava o PSDB na centro-esquerda quando de sua criação (...) A estória torna-se outra após 1994, com a chegada do PSDB à presidência. Uma retórica de superação das divisões ideológicas clássicas (...) foi um dos fundamentos justificativos da grande aliança parlamentar com partidos de centro e direita (...). Tanto que, após a eleição presidencial de 1994, a maioria dos analistas passou a classificar o PSDB como partido de centro junto com o PMDB. --> Most analysts defined PSDB as center-left as of its foundation (...) The story changed after 1994, with the election of PSDB to the Presidency. A rhetoric of overcoming the classical ideological divisions (...) was one of the justifications for the grand parliamentary alliance center and right-wing parties (...). As a matter of fact, after the 1994 election, most analysts starting defining PSDB as a centrist party along with PMDB|doi-access= free }}</ref> [[Brazilian Social Democratic Party|Social Democratic Party]] – was ahead of [[Dilma Rousseff]], pre-candidate for the ruling [[center-left]] bloc led by the Workers' Party. Rousseff, however, increased her popularity greatly, rising from 3% in March 2008 to 30% in March 2010. On the May 8, 2010 poll by Vox Populi, she finally surpassed Serra, achieving 37% of the voting intention.

Another potential candidate for the ruling center-left group was [[Ciro Gomes]] from the [[Brazilian Socialist Party]],<ref name="Col"/> who lost his comfortable second place in polls to Rousseff in May 2009. After that, he maintained an average of 12% of voting intention. On April 27, 2010, Gomes' party declined to launch his candidacy, instead supporting Rousseff.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://oglobo.globo.com/pais/mat/2010/04/27/ciro-gomes-diz-que-decisao-do-psb-foi-erro-tatico-916446222.asp|title = Ciro Gomes diz que decisão do PSB foi 'erro tático'|date = 27 April 2010}}</ref> In the left-wing opposition group, [[Socialism and Freedom Party]]'s [[Heloísa Helena (politician)|Heloísa Helena]] was the most likely candidate, but her name was withdrawn from polling after she decided to run for a seat in the Senate for [[Alagoas]].<ref name="US">{{in lang|pt}} Faria, Tales. [http://ultimosegundo.ig.com.br/brasil/2009/12/08/psol+aprova+resolucao+para+se+afastar+de+marina+silva+9227625.html "PSol aprova resolução para se afastar de Marina Silva"]. ''Último Segundo''. December 8, 2009.</ref> Plínio de Arruda Sampaio was her party's candidate for president.<ref name="US" /> Almost simultaneously, [[Marina Silva]] left the Workers' Party and joined the [[Green Party (Brazil)|Green Party]] to run for president.<ref>{{in lang|pt}} [[O Estado de S. Paulo|Agência Estado]]. [http://g1.globo.com/Noticias/Politica/0,,MUL1267346-5601,00-PV+JA+ARTICULA+APOIO+A+CANDIDATURA+DE+MARINA+SILVA.html "PV já articula apoio à candidatura de Marina Silva"]. August 14, 2009. [[Globo.com]]. Retrieved on 2009-08-15.</ref> Prior to her candidature, she was well known internationally as a defender of the [[Amazon rainforest]], but was less known in her native Brazil.<ref name="Col" />

==Polls==
The results displayed in this article excludes results for spontaneous polls (in which cards with the names of likely candidates are not presented to researched voters), due to the significant number of voters that would vote for [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]]. By law, leaders of all stances of the [[Executive branch]] can only be re-elected once.

In September, Vox Populi institute began an unprecedented [[tracking poll]] for president, which was intended to last for 36 days until October 2.
